commitResults.messageTitle: Replace address and tags in Person with contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Person now has a name, optional phone, optional email and a required,
non-empty set of contexts. Address and tags are removed from Person.

- Person: phone and email are Optional; at least one context is required;
  isSamePerson treats two persons as the same when they share a phone or
  an email, and ignores the name.
- Add and edit commands and their parsers use c/ for contexts; add only
  requires a name and at least one context. An empty c/ on edit is rejected.
- Storage: JsonAdaptedPerson saves and loads contexts and allows a missing
  phone or email. Add JsonAdaptedContext.
- UI, messages and sample data show contexts instead of address and tags.
- Update tests, test helpers and JSON test data to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make saving safer and keep a backup of an unreadable data file
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil.writeToFile now writes to a temporary file and moves it over the
target, so an interrupted save no longer leaves a half-written data file.

When the address book data file cannot be loaded, MainApp copies it to
<name>.bak before starting with an empty address book, so the next save does
not overwrite the original. Add FileUtil.backUp and tests for both changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the unused logger from PersonListPanel
Recover from null entries in the data file and rename an unreadable file to a timestamped backup
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with a null inside it (a null person, a null context, or a file
that only contains null) used to escape as a NullPointerException, which was
not caught by the DataLoadingException recovery in MainApp, so the app
crashed at startup. These cases now throw IllegalValueException or
DataLoadingException and take the normal recovery path.

FileUtil.backUp now renames the unreadable data file to
<name>.<UTC time>.bak instead of copying it to <name>.bak. The original name is
free for the next save, and an earlier backup keeps its own name. backUp takes
an optional Clock so tests can fix the time.

Add regression tests and fixture files for the null cases, and update the
backup tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the User Guide for the new saving behaviour
commitResults.messageBody:
Describe how a save is written, what a saved person looks like in the data
file, and what happens when the data file cannot be read: it is renamed to
addressbook.json.<UTC time>.bak and the app starts empty. Add steps to
recover the data and an FAQ entry for an unexpectedly empty list.
Make saving safer and keep a backup of an unreadable data file

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an archived flag to Person and the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A Person now knows whether it is archived. The flag is part of equals,
hashCode and toString but not of isSamePerson, so an archived person still
blocks a duplicate phone number or email. Person.withArchived returns a copy
with only the flag changed, and EditCommand keeps the flag when it edits a
person.

The data file gets an optional "archived" key. A missing or null key means
the person is not archived, so existing data files load unchanged. Any value
that is not true or false makes the file unreadable and takes the normal
backup-and-start-empty path.

Nothing in the app uses the flag yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the archive, archives and unarchive commands
commitResults.messageBody:
archive INDEX marks the contact at INDEX as archived, so it leaves the normal
contact list but stays in the address book and in the data file. archives
shows only the archived contacts under an "Archives" header, and unarchive
INDEX brings a contact back. Command words are case-insensitive, and INDEX
refers to the list on screen, as for delete.

The normal contact list now shows only contacts that are not archived: list,
add and edit return to it, it is the list shown at start-up, and find searches
only within it. The archives view is the same filtered list with a different
predicate, so no extra view state is stored. unarchive refuses a contact that
is not archived and says to run archives first.

ModelManager exposes whether the archives are shown so that the window can
show the header. The header is shown only for the archives predicate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep archived contacts safe from clear and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
clear now removes only the contacts that are not archived and goes back to the
normal contact list, so one clear cannot wipe the archive. It says how many
archived contacts were kept.

edit rejects an archived contact and asks the user to unarchive it first.
Before, the edit went through and the contact then disappeared from the
archives view.

delete is unchanged: it removes whichever contact is shown, so it deletes an
archived contact while the archives are shown. Add a test for that.

the two predicates in the Model and Storage components, add an Archive feature
section with the design alternatives that were considered, add manual test
cases and a glossary entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add archive and unarchive by context
commitResults.messageBody:
archive c/CONTEXT archives every person with that context, and
unarchive c/CONTEXT unarchives every archived person with it. Both work on
the whole address book, not the displayed list, and match the context
exactly, ignoring capitalisation.

SetArchivedByContextCommand holds the shared steps; ArchiveByContextCommand
and UnarchiveByContextCommand only set the target state and messages.
ContextArgumentParser lets both parsers tell the c/ form from an index, and
rejects c/ combined with an index, another prefix or a second c/.

Update the user guide, the developer guide (with sequence, activity and class
diagrams) and the manual testing steps.

- UniquePersonList: find the chosen person by identity first, so archive,
  edit, delete and unarchive no longer act on an equal twin elsewhere in
  the list
- LogicManager: skip saving for commands that change nothing, and name the
  data file, not a temp file, in the permission error
- AddressBookParser: match line separators in arguments so a note error is
  reported instead of the help usage
- Note: reject Unicode line and paragraph separators
- StringUtil: accept ASCII digits only in indexes
- FileUtil: keep both backups when two fail in the same second
- HelpWindow: link to this team's user guide, not AB3's

  document the failed-save behaviour

commitResults.messageTitle: Show specific errors for empty name and context
commitResults.messageBody:
An empty n/ or c/ used to fail the format regex and show the full

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the clashing person in duplicate add errors

A duplicate add showed the generic "This person already exists in the

UniquePersonList#findDuplicate returns the first person in the list

commitResults.messageBody:

to the model in #98, and the loss is saved to the data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that edit keeps alias, introducer and note
commitResults.messageBody:

in scope instead of get(0) and Index.fromOneBased(1).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add +c/ and -c/ prefixes for editing contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit will add or remove one context at a time instead of replacing
all of them with c/.

Let's define the two prefixes so the edit parser can use them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add and remove single contexts in edit
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit replaces every context with the c/ values, so changing one
context means retyping all of them.

Let's replace c/ with +c/ and -c/, which add or remove one context
at a time. Removals run before additions, so a person's only context
can be swapped and its capitalisation fixed in one command. The
command is rejected if a -c/ context is not found or no context
would remain, and plain c/ is rejected with a hint.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the typed order of edit contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contexts are parsed into a HashSet, so an error listing several
unmatched -c/ contexts shows them in an unpredictable order.

Let's use a LinkedHashSet so they keep the order the user typed.
While here, fix the setter Javadocs that still referred to the old
contexts field, and test that +c/ keeps the existing spelling of a
context the person already has.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add -p/ and -e/ prefixes to remove phone and email
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone and email are optional, but edit cannot remove them once set.
An empty p/ or e/ is rejected. Letting it clear the field instead
would wipe the phone if the user presses Enter before typing it.

Let's define explicit remove prefixes so the edit parser can use them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track phone and email removal in edit descriptor
commitResults.messageBody:
A null phone or email in EditPersonDescriptor means the user did not
type p/ or e/, so it cannot also mean the field should be removed.

Let's add separate flags for removing the phone and email, so the
parser can record -p/ and -e/ and the command can act on them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove phone or email when edit asks for it
commitResults.messageBody:
EditPersonDescriptor can now mark the phone or email for removal, but
createEditedPerson still keeps the old value.

Let's leave the field empty when it is marked for removal, so the
edited person has no phone or email.

Edit can now remove a phone or email, but the parser does not read
the -p/ and -e/ prefixes yet.

Let's parse them and reject -p/ with a value, p/ and -p/ together,
and an empty p/, with the same checks for email. The empty p/ error
now points to -p/, so users know how to remove the field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that removing phone and email skips the duplicate check
commitResults.messageBody:
Two people without a phone or email must not count as duplicates,
otherwise removing these fields from a second person would fail.

Let's add a test where both people end up with neither field.

The edit usage message needs to show the new edit prefixes, which
are defined in #116 and #117 but not merged yet.

Let's define the same four prefixes here, identical to those PRs, so
the usage message can use them and the branches merge cleanly.

The usage message still says existing values are overwritten, shows
c/ and does not explain what INDEX is. An edit with no fields shows
only the error, without how to use edit.

Let's show the new parameters, explain INDEX and -p/ / -e/, and add
the usage message to the no-field error.

The edit section still describes address and tags, and says
contexts are replaced.

Let's describe the new format, +c/ / -c/ and -p/ / -e/, with
examples, the success message, duplicates and every error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add separate phone and email examples to edit errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Rows covering both phone and email errors showed only a phone
example, so the email message had no matching command.

Let's give each message its own example.

Collectors.toSet() does not keep insertion order, unlike the
LinkedHashSet used by ParserUtil.parseContexts. Tests that depend on
context order could then be nondeterministic.

Let's collect contexts into a LinkedHashSet instead.

commitResults.messageBody:

Let's link the two in their Javadoc so they stay in sync.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions for the run task
commitResults.messageBody:
Gradle enables assertions for the test task by default, but not for
the run task, so assert statements are skipped when the app is
launched via gradlew run.

Let's set enableAssertions for the run task so assertions are checked
during manual runs too.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add activity diagram for edit phone prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG does not show the phone rules that edit gained in #105. p/
sets the phone and -p/ removes it, and edit rejects repeated
prefixes, -p/ with a value, both prefixes together, an empty p/ and
an invalid phone. The checks run in a fixed order, and that order
decides which error the user sees when a command breaks more than one
rule.

Let's add an activity diagram of these checks in a new "Edit feature"
section, and note that e/ and -e/ follow the same rules.

An activity diagram suits these rules because they are branching
logic. A sequence diagram of edit would mostly repeat the existing
delete diagram. Contexts are left out until #109 changes how unmatched
-c/ contexts are handled.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Quote real empty-phone error in edit diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit phone activity diagram labels the empty-phone error as
"phone cannot be empty", but edit shows "Phone number cannot be
empty". A quoted label reads as the exact message, so let's quote the
message the user sees.

Edit parses the phone and the email with two copies of the same
checks: a value after the remove prefix, the set and remove prefixes
together, and an empty set prefix. Each copy says that a change to one
must be made to the other.

Edit will also set and remove the alias, introducer and note (#110),
which would make five copies to keep in step.

Let's move the checks into one helper. Each removable field calls it
with its prefixes, its parser and how error messages name the field.

The messages users see stay word for word. The tests now check the
message text, as the per-field message constants are gone.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommand: Share how optional fields are edited
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit works out the new phone and the new email with the same
expression: no value if the field is removed, else the new value if
given, else the current one.

Edit will apply this to the alias, introducer and note too (#110).

Let's move the expression into one helper that each optional field
uses, so the rule is written once.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add alias, introducer and note to edit descriptor
commitResults.messageBody:
A person may have an alias, an introducer and a note (#98), but edit
copies them over unchanged, as EditPersonDescriptor has no way to
change them.

Let's let the descriptor set or remove each of the three, in the same
way as the phone and the email, and apply the changes with the shared
helper in EditCommand.

The parser does not fill in these fields yet, so users see no change
until the prefixes are added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let edit set and remove alias, introducer and note
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit cannot change a person's alias, introducer or note (#110), so a
typo in one of them can only be fixed by deleting and re-adding the
person.

Let's accept a/, i/ and nt/ in edit to set or replace each field,
with the same rules and errors as in add. Let's also add -a/, -i/ and
-nt/ to remove each field, following -p/ and -e/: the remove prefix
takes no value, cannot be given with its set prefix, and an empty set
prefix points to it.

i/ is now an edit prefix, so the preamble test uses t/ as its example
of a prefix that edit does not know.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Document editing alias, introducer and note
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit now sets alias, introducer and note with a/, i/ and nt/, and
removes them with -a/, -i/ and -nt/, but the User Guide covers only
the phone and email prefixes.

Let's add the new prefixes to the format, rules, examples, error
table and command summary, so users can find them without trying
each prefix.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap edit lines over the soft length limit
commitResults.messageBody:
Some lines added for #110 are 111 to 116 characters long, over the
coding standard's soft limit of 110.

Let's wrap them, so the edit code stays within the soft limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note contexts skipped by +c/ in edit
commitResults.messageBody:
When +c/ names a context the person already has, edit skips it and
keeps the existing spelling, but the success message does not say so.
Users who typed a context with different capitalisation may think it
was added or respelt.

Let's add a note on a new line of the success message that lists every
skipped context, spelt the way the person has it, in the order typed.

A context is only counted as skipped if the person still has it after
the -c/ removals, so removing and re-adding a context to change its
spelling shows no note.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Document note for skipped +c/ contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit section says a +c/ context the person already has changes
nothing, but not that the result display now lists such contexts.

Let's mention the note in the matching rules and show an example of it
under the success output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show message when edit changes nothing
commitResults.messageBody:
A valid edit that leaves the person as they were, such as re-entering
the current phone number or adding a context the person already has,
still shows "Edited person", so the user cannot tell that nothing
happened.

Let's show "No changes made to <Name>." instead, without saving.

Person#equals cannot be used to detect this, as it ignores case in
emails and contexts. A capitalisation fix such as e/Alice@Example.com
must count as a change and be saved, so let's compare the exact
spelling of each field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Redraw person card when only case changes
commitResults.messageBody:
ListCell skips redrawing a cell when the new item equals the old one.
Person#equals ignores case in emails and contexts, so after an edit
that only fixes their capitalisation, the card keeps showing the old
spelling.

Let's treat any new Person object as a changed item, so the card is
redrawn after every edit.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Document no-changes message for edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit section does not mention what is shown when an edit changes
nothing.

Let's describe the "No changes made" message, and that a change in
capitalisation counts as a change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Skip unmatched contexts in edit with a note
commitResults.messageBody:
An edit with a -c/ context the person does not have is rejected as a
whole. A typo in one context then throws away every other change in
the command.

Let's skip unmatched -c/ contexts instead, and add a note listing them
after the success message. Skipped contexts are never removed, so they
do not count when checking that the person keeps at least one context.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Document skipped -c/ contexts in edit
DeveloperGuide: Note edit activity applies to all optional fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The activity diagram only shows phone, which may suggest the other
optional fields behave differently.

Let's state that the same activity applies to every optional field
prefix, so readers do not need a diagram per field.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommandParser: Pass remove flag as primitive boolean
commitResults.messageBody:
parseOptionalField takes the remove flag setter as a Consumer<Boolean>,
which boxes the flag only for the descriptor setter to unbox it again.

Let's add a RemovalSetter interface that takes a primitive boolean, and
comment each stage of parseOptionalField so the order of its checks is
clear.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Split edit format across lines
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit format line now lists every set and remove prefix, so it runs
far past the page width and is hard to scan.

Let's split it into set, remove and context prefixes, and note that the
command is still typed on one line.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommandTest: Test skipped-context note after a rename
commitResults.messageBody:
The skipped-context note names the person after the edit, so an n/
rename in the same command shows the new name. No test covers this, so
a switch to the old name would go unnoticed.

Let's add a test that renames a person and adds a context they already
have, and checks the note uses the new name.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommand: Build no-change check on Person#equals
commitResults.messageBody:
hasSameDetails compares each Person field one by one. A field added to
Person later would be left out, so an edit to only that field would
show "No changes made" and not be saved.

Person#equals already compares every field, but ignores case in emails
and contexts, so it cannot be used alone.

Let's use Person#equals and add exact-spelling checks for emails and
contexts only, so new fields are compared without changing this method.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommand: Rename unmatched-context message to show it is a note
commitResults.messageBody:
MESSAGE_CONTEXTS_NOT_FOUND was named when an unmatched -c/ context
rejected the command. The command now skips the context and adds a
note, so the name reads like an error that no longer happens.

Let's rename it to MESSAGE_CONTEXTS_NOT_FOUND_SKIPPED, matching
MESSAGE_CONTEXTS_SKIPPED for contexts skipped by +c/.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Warn that misspelt -c/ contexts are skipped
commitResults.messageBody:
An unmatched -c/ context no longer rejects the command, so a typo
lets the rest of the edit go through. The edit section only says the
context is skipped and listed in a note.

Let's tell users to check the note for typos.

commitResults.messageBody:
The window title still showed the AB3 name 'Address App' on every
launch. Replace it with the product name in MainWindow.fxml.

commitResults.messageTitle: Messages: Hint when duplicate person is archived
commitResults.messageBody:
The duplicate error names the clashing person but does not say they
are archived, so users cannot find them with list or find. Append a
hint pointing to archives when the existing person is archived. The
message for non-archived persons is unchanged. Update the UG add and
edit duplicate descriptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add: warn when identical contact already exists
commitResults.messageBody:
A person with no phone or email is never a duplicate, so adding the
same name and contexts twice silently created identical entries.
Still add the person, but append a note to the success message when
an existing phone-less, email-less person has the same name (ignoring
case and repeated spaces) and the same contexts. Document the note in
the UG duplicate persons section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Match names saved with repeated spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
The clue had its spaces collapsed but the stored name and context did
not, so a name such as 'Alex  Tan' could never match a full-name clue.
Collapse whitespace runs on both sides before comparing; stored names
are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: make nt/ take the rest of the line
commitResults.messageBody:
A note containing text such as " n/", " a/" or " c/o" was split at
that point by ArgumentTokenizer, so the remainder silently overwrote
the name, alias or contexts. Notes are the only free-text field, so
shorthand like "c/o", "n/a" or "p/t" is likely.

Add ArgumentTokenizer#tokenizeWithLastPrefix, which cuts the arguments
at the first " nt/" and takes everything after it as the note. add and
edit use it, so nt/ must now be the last parameter. -nt/ is a separate
prefix and still works. Update the add/edit usage messages, the UG note
rule and the edit example that put nt/ before -i/.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: show nt/ last in edit usage and UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous commit made nt/ take the rest of the line, so it must be
the last parameter. Move [nt/NOTE] to the end of the edit usage message
and the UG edit format and summary rows, note the exception to "any
order", and say a second nt/ becomes part of the note instead of
raising a duplicate-prefix error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add: mention archived in identical contact note
commitResults.messageBody:
When the identical existing person is archived, the user cannot see
them in the list, so the note alone is confusing. Append a hint to run
archives. An active identical person takes precedence, in which case no
hint is shown. Document the archived case in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add: warn on same name and shared context
commitResults.messageBody:
The note only fired for identical name and contexts on persons with no
phone or email, so likely duplicates were missed. Now warn when the new
person has no phone or email and any existing person, whatever their
phone or email, has the same name and at least one shared context.
Active matches are preferred over archived ones. The note shows the
shared contexts and, for active matches, the index to use with edit.
Update the UG duplicate persons section.

tokenizeWithLastPrefix takes a prefix whose value runs to the end of
the line. "Last" reads as the last occurrence of that prefix, but the
method cuts the arguments at its first occurrence.

Let's rename it to tokenizeWithRestOfLinePrefix, along with its
parameter and local variables, so the name says what the prefix's
value is rather than where the prefix sits.

tokenizeWithRestOfLinePrefix puts exactly one value for nt/, as any
later nt/ becomes part of that value. The duplicate-prefix check for
nt/ in add and edit can no longer fail, yet listing nt/ there suggests
a repeated nt/ is still rejected.

Let's remove nt/ from both duplicate checks so the code matches the
documented behaviour. -nt/ is still checked, as it is tokenized
normally.

commitResults.messageTitle: Messages: Build archived hint sentence in method
commitResults.messageBody:
The archived hint constant starts with a space so that it can be
appended straight after the duplicate person message. That space is
easy to lose when the text is edited or reused elsewhere.

Let's store the hint without the leading space and add the space
where the message is built. Let's also rename the constant to
MESSAGE_ARCHIVED_PERSON_HINT, as the hint is not tied to the duplicate
person message and can be shared by other messages about archived
persons.

The UG quotes the hint without the leading space to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test archived duplicate hint at command level
commitResults.messageBody:
MessagesTest checks the archived hint text, but not that add and edit
find archived persons as duplicates and show the hint to the user.

Let's add a test to AddCommandIntegrationTest and EditCommandTest in
which the clash is with an archived person. Both use a real
ModelManager, so they also cover Model#findDuplicate with and without
a person to skip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Normalise each clue once via shared helper
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonMatchesCluesPredicate normalises every clue again for each
person it tests, recompiling the whitespace regex each time.
FindCommandParser has its own copy of the same whitespace-collapsing
code, and the duplicate-contact check in #180 needs it too.

Let's add StringUtil#collapseWhitespace, backed by a precompiled
Pattern, and use it in both places. The predicate now normalises its
clues once in the constructor, so test() only normalises the person's
fields.

Predicates whose clues differ only in case or spacing are now equal,
as they match the same persons, and toString() shows the normalised
clues.

commitResults.messageTitle: AddCommand: Add note newline where note is added
commitResults.messageBody:
The similar person note constants start with a newline, which is easy
to miss when reading or reusing them.

Let's keep only the note text in the constants and add the newline
where the note is appended to the success message, as EditCommand does
for its notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: AddCommand: Show new entry's index in note
commitResults.messageBody:
The note for an active similar person tells the user to delete the new
entry, but not where the new entry is, so they must find it first.

Let's include its index, e.g. "run delete 10 to remove the new entry".
The new entry is always after the existing person in the list, so
deleting it first does not shift the index to use with edit.

The new entry is looked up by identity rather than equals, because a
person with no phone or email can be equal to the existing person,
which would give the existing person's index instead.

Update the UG example to match.
